Gravity when not jumping, on screens that have it ($45FF): every $534B (12) calls try to move the boy down a pixel. If he moved he is falling: count it ($534E), play the fall whistle (fall_sound) and lock up and down ($4502/$4503 = 0). If not, he stands: silence and land.

The boy's vertical motion, called every pass from tick_border. Not jumping ($C19C = 0): gravity (fall_step). Jumping: when the step timer $2A7F runs out move one pixel, up while rising ($C19B = 0) and down while falling. Rising, jump_counter $2A7E counts up and each step waits jump_speeds[counter], so the rise slows; after 24 steps, or when a ceiling stops him, he falls. Falling, the counter counts back down the same table, so the fall speeds up, until it reaches 0 or the ground stops him. The sound's pitch follows ($54FC, $5518).
jump_step's timer ran out: a rising step (remember_y, up one pixel, rise_blocked, the next time from jump_speeds, the pitch) or, when falling, $53C6.
jump_step falling: fall_blocked, the counter down; at 0 the jump ends ($53E2), else the next time from jump_speeds and the pitch.
The jump is over: $C19C = 0, fall count $18, so start_jump waits for land.
Standing: allow up and down again ($4502/$4503 = 1) and clear the fall count $534E. A compare of the fall with $457A is followed only by NOPs, so there is no fall damage (and $457A is $FF).

After a rising step: an unchanged Y means a ceiling stopped him, so he falls from here ($C19B = 1). Count the step (jump_counter).

Passes between steps of a jump, by jump_counter 0-24: 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 31, 34, 37, 41, 45. Read forwards rising and backwards falling: a slowing rise and a quickening fall.
Sprite 0's Y before a falling step (fall_blocked).
One falling step; an unchanged Y means he has landed: the jump is over ($C19C = 0).
Start the jump sound on SID voice 3: attack/decay $0D, sustain/release 0, waveform $45B7 ($11: triangle, gate on), frequency $0800 ($54EA); then walk_frame.
1 while the falling whistle is playing.
Silence voice 3, forget the whistle ($549F = 0), then land.
The falling whistle on voice 3: the first call starts it at $8080, each later call lowers the frequency by $80 ($54C1).
The falling whistle's frequency, high byte.
The falling whistle's frequency, low byte.
The falling whistle's next step: frequency down by $80.
fall_sound's first call: the whistle starts at $8080.
Per enemy slot: its frame delay, from the record; speed_up halves it.
Slots 1-4's frame delays, from the record.
Slots 2-4's frame delays (with $54E5).
Slots 3 and 4's frame delays.
Slot 4's frame delay.
The jump sound's starting frequency, $0800, then walk_frame.
The jump sound's frequency, low byte.
The jump sound's frequency, high byte.
A rising step: the jump sound's frequency ($54F9/$54FA) drops by 5.

A falling step: the frequency's low byte rises by 5, but the BCS at $5524 branches to the next instruction, so the high byte is decremented every time: the pitch falls by about 256 per step instead of rising. A slip in the code.

Code that would reset sprites 0 and 1 to the stored start and draw a box of glyphs; called only from the card text read as code ($4345, $43B4, $4278). Not reached in play: no simulator run on any of the ten screens read or ran it, and the only instructions that name it are the card text read as code ($41xx-$43xx), the unused tools, or the RAM under the KERNAL.

Set try_move's row offset (the SBC operand at $2A0C) for the current screen: with gravity ($45FF = 1) $2C and down blocked from above ($4500 = 0, via $570A), without it $30. Then reload the enemy frames ($2F47).
Keep the slot being spawned in $C0E3 and set its moving flag $CF33,x = 1.
Each slot's lives from $45E7 into $CF76, and sprite 0's pointer from $45EC.
Each LEVEL makes the enemies faster: for each slot whose move delay ($CF9C) is not already the value at $34E8, halve it (to at least 1) and halve its frame delay ($54E5, to at least 2).
Enemy slot X's move delay (A) into $CF9C,x and its frame delay from $4548,x into $54E5,x.
enemy_lives_reset, from new_life.
copy_block descriptor: the HUD rows $8400-$844F to $0400, used when a new game starts (start_game $C672).
Unreached, 68 bytes: no call, jump or absolute access names them and no simulator run executed or read them. They decode as rts rts rts rts rts ...: code or data left over from development.
gravity_setup's two branches. With gravity: $4501 (down allowed) = 0 and try_move subtracts $2C; without: $30. Both reload the first path direction ($2F47).
Clear the first 1 KB of the character set ($3000-$33FF). Called by nothing in play.
Three NOPs where show_game_over's call lands, then show_press_ctrl.
show_press_ctrl: loads PRESS CTRL FOR MENU and screen/colour bytes for row 23 but stores nothing (every access is LDA): the message never appears. Called only through $5733.

"PRESS CTRL FOR MENU", screen codes + $80. Copied to screen row 23 by show_press_ctrl;
no JSR to that routine was found, so where it is used is open.
Per enemy slot: low byte of its path script's address (high byte at $CF24,x), from the record.
Slots 1-4's path script low bytes (with $575E).
Slots 2-4's path script low bytes (with $575E).
Slots 3 and 4's path script low bytes.
Slot 4's path script low byte.
A JMP to switch_allowed, for switch_request.

Swap the boy and the girl: wait for raster line 16, swap the two sprites (swap_sprites), both on; patch the frame numbers in read_controls, walk_frame and jump_lockout to the other character's sprites ($E8-$F6 for the girl, $D8-$E6 for the boy); flip $5A08 and set the border, 10 (light red) for the girl, 6 (blue) for the boy.
Unreached, 9 bytes: no call, jump or absolute access names them and no simulator run executed or read them. They decode as nop nop nop nop nop ...: code or data left over from development.

Once per main-loop pass: count the pass ($CF02), the energy-bar speed check (bar_speed), the energy and poison timers (energy_tick). In a jump, put the take-off direction back ($5A01 -> $C1ED). On the ground, switch read_controls and frame_step back on, check fire for a player switch (switch_request) and reset the jump frames. Then drain_step. Returns $CF02 for main_loop.
player_step's frame numbers for the ground, patched by player_swap ($D8/$DC boy, $E8/$EC girl).
player_step's ground frame for walking right (patched), then drain_step.
Unreached, 11 bytes: no call, jump or absolute access names them and no simulator run executed or read them. They decode as nop nop nop nop nop ...: code or data left over from development.
When sprite 0's X has not changed for $90 passes ($5A03), show the standing frame for the facing ($E2 or $E6; patched by player_swap).
idle_frame's frame numbers ($E1/$E6 for the boy, $F1/$F6 for the girl, patched by player_swap), then the stand-still counter.
idle_frame's first frame number (patched).
idle_frame's stand-still test: X unchanged for $90 passes shows the standing frame.
idle_frame's standing frames (patched by player_swap), stored into sprite 0.
idle_frame's second standing frame (patched).

While in the air: read_controls and frame_step are switched off (their first bytes become RTS, $60), the horizontal direction held at take-off is kept ($5A01, put back each pass by player_step), the jumping frame is shown ($E0 or $E1 by facing) and the jump sound starts (jump_sound).
jump_lockout's frame numbers ($E0/$E1 for the boy, $F0/$F1 for the girl), then the jump sound.
jump_lockout's second frame number (patched), then the jump sound.
jump_lockout's frame bases for player_input (patched), then the jump sound.
Switch players: X = 1 for the stick's fire bit or key code $37 ('/', the ? key; live: $C5 = $37 swapped to the girl, border 6 -> 10, on the way back and did nothing in the forest).
switch_request continued: fire (bit 4 of $DC00) or '?' ($C5 = $37); the first press after a release goes to switch_allowed.
Swap sprite 0 and sprite 1: X, Y, their X MSB bits and their pointers ($07F8/$07F9). The character under control is always sprite 0.
For a new game: reset the score line (hud_reset $2CA4), put sprite 1 off-screen at $E0,$E0, the border blue and sprite 1's pointer $EE.
swap_sprites continued: sprite 1's old Y to sprite 0, the X MSB bits exchanged, then the two pointers.

The boy slows down as his energy goes. While the bar's seventh cell ($0430) is full: input every $20 passes and a frame step every 2 ($5A88). Once it is not: input only every $80 passes ($CA19 patches main_loop's compare) and a frame step every 4 ($450C).
Step sprite 0's pointer $07F8 to the next of its four frames (the low two bits wrap from 3 to 0).
Find the end of the energy bar: the first cell from $042E (screen row 1, column 6) that is not a full block ($A9). Returns its index in X.

Take one eighth-cell off the energy bar: step the last partial cell's glyph down ($A8 ... $A1); when it is empty move to the cell before. When the bar is gone (index 0, glyph $A1) the boy has no energy: out_of_energy $5A70.
energy_down at an empty cell: step back a cell, or with none left out_of_energy.
energy_down: the bar is gone, out_of_energy.
Add one step to the energy bar, up to 33 cells ($21); when the bar is already full, score 10 instead ($CF5A = $0A, add_score).
energy_up with a full bar: 10 points instead.
The energy cost of moving: in a jump, one step off the bar when $5A09 counts to zero; walking, walk_drain. Standing still costs nothing.
1 while a jump holds the take-off direction; player_step then puts $5A01 back into $C1ED each pass.
The horizontal direction at take-off, kept for the whole jump.
Sprite 0's X on the last pass, for idle_frame.
Passes the boy has stood still; at $90 idle_frame shows the standing frame.
1 once a switch has been asked for, until fire and '?' are released (switch_request).
Working copy of $D010 while swap_sprites exchanges sprites 0's and 1's MSB bits.
Who is being controlled: 0 the boy, 1 the girl. Sets the border colour (6 or 10) and which crosses may be taken (cross_touch).
Energy cost counter while in the air (drain_step).
Walking cost counter, inner (walk_drain).
Walking cost counter, outer (every 3 of the inner).
Energy still to be added, one bar step per 16 calls (energy_tick): a mushroom adds 23.
energy_tick's 16-call timer.
tile_touch_a's crumble timer: every 8th step on a crumbling ledge changes its glyph.
energy_add_slow's loop count.
Poison still to be spent, one bar step per 18 calls (poison_tick): a toadstool adds 24, an enemy touch 1.
poison_tick's 18-call timer.
poison_add's loop count.
Sinking timer for tiles $62-$65: he falls through them on every 3rd try.
Crosses still needed on this screen (crosses_left); from +$72 of the record.
colour_cycle's 40-call timer.
While a horizontal direction is held ($C1ED), count $5A0A down from 255 and $5A0B from 3; at zero take one step off the bar (energy_down): about one step per 765 passes of walking.
Between screens: keep the HUD across the card (hud_restore $7659), then set the border to the current player's colour (6 the boy, 10 the girl).
One-off setup after loading: walking frame every 2nd call ($450C = 2), then the screen setup at $5D80.
The energy is gone: set the screen-over flag $CF7D (read by collect_check, which plays the end jingle and goes to game over), and slow the walking animation ($450C = 2, $CA19 = $20).
bar_speed with a full bar: frame every 2nd call, input every $20 passes.

Tiles $2A-$53 in the probed cell. Below $4D: solid, he does not move (the RTS at $5AAA). $4D-$53 with the probe to the side: he moves. $4D-$53 below his feet (Y = $50): every 8th try ($5A0F) the tile steps to the next glyph, and $53 becomes a space: a crumbling ledge that gives way under him after seven steps.
tile_touch_a on a crumbling ledge: reset the 8-step timer; $53 becomes a space, other stages step on ($5ABF).
tile_touch_a: a crumbling ledge steps to its next glyph.

Tiles $54 and up under the boy. $54: an edible mushroom: add 24 to the energy-drain counter's opposite, energy_add_slow $5B18 (X = $18), and remove the tile. $55: a poisonous toadstool: poison_add $5B44 (X = $19) and remove it. $56: a bonus: score +100 ($CF5A = $64, add_score $CE42) and remove it. $57: a magic cross (cross_touch $7F50). The rest decide whether he may move: $58-$61 and $66 up (via $7673 for $70 up) are solid underfoot, so with the probe below (Y = $50) he does not move and otherwise he does; $62-$65 are solid from the side and give way below only on every 3rd try ($5A14), so he sinks through them slowly.
Every 16th call while energy is pending ($5A0D > 0): take one unit and grow the energy bar by one step (energy_up $59C3). Then poison_tick.
Add X-1 to the pending energy gain $5A0D (stopping at 255). energy_tick $5B00 later turns each unit into one step of the energy bar, one every 16 calls.
Every 18th call while poison is pending ($5A11 > 0): take one unit and run flash_border $72BA, which also takes a step off the energy bar.

Add X-1 to the pending poison $5A11 (stopping at 255). poison_tick $5B2C later spends it, one unit every 18 calls, each one flashing the border (flash_border $72BA). Called by the toadstool, by an enemy touching the boy ($CDC0) and by the girl touching one ($CEC7).
tile_touch_b's cross test ($57, cross_touch), then the floor tests.
One more cross: step the two-digit MAGIC CROSSES counter on screen ($041C tens, $041D units, glyphs $B0-$B9), then crosses_left $7F00.
Wait for raster line 16 ($D012 = $10 with bit 8 clear), above the visible screen.
copy_block descriptor: $B200-$B5FE to $3000, the font the cards and the title use.

Show this screen's card: the title font back (copy_block $5BBF: $B200-$B5FE to $3000), sprites off, multicolours black, the card named by +$74 of the level record (show_card), then the card tune from $6A18 until it signals (card_wait $7610).
The logo drawer's column counter: show_card's $5C00 draws the big CHILLER letters in 5-row strips until it reaches $6A.
Cleared by the logo drawer; nothing reads it.
The logo drawer's letter step: after every 5 strips the glyph jumps back by $63.
The logo drawer's column within a letter (0-2).
The glyph the logo drawer puts next, starting at $E7.

Draw the big CHILLER logo on a card: glyphs from $E7 upward, five rows deep, from screen row 1 ($0545) with colour $0A (red) in colour RAM ($D945), three columns per letter; the letter shapes are glyphs of the title font.

Show a card: print it, black border and background, multicolour text on, charset at $3000
($D018 = $1C), then stamp "MASTERTRONIC'S" (screen codes + $80, 14 bytes) at $04D6, which is
screen row 5, column 14, in red.
The next glyph for draw_logo: +$19 within a letter's strip, back $63 at a new letter (every 5).
Count the logo's columns and stop at $6A; the last cell gets glyph $32 in colour $0A.
Clear draw_logo's counters before a card.

Print a text card. X/Y = card address. Clears the screen (CHR$(147)), puts the cursor at
the card's first two bytes (row, column) through KERNAL PLOT, then prints PETSCII through
CHROUT up to a $01 terminator. Colour and cursor control codes lay the card out.
MASTERTRONIC'S (without the apostrophe, which card_apostrophe adds a row higher), screen codes + $80, 13 bytes; show_card copies 14.
An older forest card: clear screen, reverse on, red, upper case, THE FOREST; show_forest_card prints it, and nothing calls that.
Unpack a screen's colour map into colour RAM $D800-$DBEF, two cells per source byte (low nibble, then high nibble). The source ($8800 as written) is patched by setup_screen from +$0C/+$0D.
unpack_colours' source operand (patched from +$0C of the level record), then the unpacking loop.
unpack_colours' source high byte (patched), then the loop.
unpack_colours' loop: two cells per byte until $DBF0.
A new game starts with the boy: $5A08 = 1 then player_swap, which flips it to 0 and sets his frames and the blue border.
Multicolour text on ($D016 bit 4), the third and fourth background colours ($D023 = 11 grey, $D024 = 1 white), then wait_ram $5E0A and gravity_setup $5651.

The energy is gone (out_of_energy set $CF7D): GAME OVER on row 1 (show_game_over), then the jingle at $6B10 (play position and loop point in zp $B7-$BA). $5DA9 waits for its count, stops the music, clears pending energy and poison, and game_over.
Wait for the jingle's count ($02FF), stop the music, clear pending energy and poison, then game_over.
Unreached, 55 bytes: no call, jump or absolute access names them and no simulator run executed or read them. They decode as cmp cmp cmp cmp cmp ...: code or data left over from development.
Print the short forest card at $5D0D. Nothing calls it: the forest's card is at $4100 like the others.
Clear bit 0 of the processor port $01 until it reads back clear: BASIC ROM out, so the RAM at $A000-$BFFF (the graphics and level data) is visible. From here on $01 = $36.

Build screen X/2 (X = 0, 2 ... $12) from its level record: zp $11/$12 = level_records[X]. Shows the card first (save_hud $5A41), then copies the play area with the KERNAL banked out ($72A4, the record's +0 descriptor) and the character set (+6), unpacks the colour map (+$0C, unpack_colours), sets the two multicolours (+$0E, +$0F), places the boy and the girl (sprites 0 and 1, +$10-+$17), loads each enemy table (five bytes each, +$18-+$44, into $CF68, $CF3D, $CF38, $45AD, $CF9C, $54E5, $45E2, $575E, $CF24) and the path table $4519 (+$45-+$5D). Then place_crosses twice (blue $0E, then red $0A; ten addresses from +$5E) and set_crosses_needed (+$72).
Place five crosses: for each of five screen addresses from the level record, write the cross tile $57 and its colour ($5FDC, patched to $0E for blue, $0A for red) into colour RAM, $D4 pages above.
place_crosses' colour operand ($0E blue, $0A red), then the colour-RAM store.

NOPs and bytes after place_crosses, up to the music player at $60A0. Not reached in play: no simulator run on any of the ten screens read or ran it, and the only instructions that name it are the card text read as code ($41xx-$43xx), the unused tools, or the RAM under the KERNAL.
The SID filter and volume for the music: cutoff $45/$05, resonance 15 with voice 1 filtered, low-pass and band-pass, volume 15.

Start the music: silence the SID, point the play position zp $B7/$B8 and the loop point
zp $B9/$BA at the tune, set the filter and volume, and install music_irq in $0314.

The IRQ ($0314): count the step timer zp $02 down; at zero play the next command. Exits
through the KERNAL's $EA31 via music_irq_exit.

Self-modified: music_next_command stores the command byte into $610C, so this JMP goes
to $61xx, the handler for that byte.
The operand music_next_command writes: the handler's low byte. The note handlers follow.
Voice 1's note: frequency high and low from the tune, gate off and on with voice 1's waveform.
Voice 2's note: frequency high and low from the tune, gate off and on with voice 2's waveform.
Both voices' notes: four tune bytes, then retrigger both.
Gate both voices off and on again with their waveforms: a repeated chord.
Set the tempo from the next tune byte, then end the step.
A rest: the step timer reloads from the tempo, nothing new sounds.
Count: INC $02FF, which the game polls ($5DAD, $7614) to learn how far the tune has got.
Voices 1 and 2's waveform bytes ($02AC, $02AD) from the next two tune bytes, then the next command.
Attack/decay for voices 1 and 2, then sustain/release for 1 and 2: four tune bytes.
Pulse widths for voices 1 and 2 (four tune bytes: lo, hi, lo, hi).
Loop: the play position goes back to the loop point.
Stop the music: silence the SID and give $0314 back to the KERNAL's $EA31.
Advance the play position and return the byte there in A.

The tune: command bytes, each the low byte of its handler's address in page $61, each
followed by its operands (see music_dispatch). Played from $61F9 (music_fetch pre-increments)
to the loop command $C7 at $6A15. Pitches are computed for the NTSC clock.
The tune continued from tune_data ($61F8), to its loop command at $6A15.
The last bytes of the play tune, up to its loop command at $6A15.
The card tune, played from $6A19 (show_level_card points the player at $6A18); it ends with the count command card_wait waits for.
The end-of-screen jingle, played from $6B11 (screen_done points the player at $6B10); its count ends the wait at $5DA9.
Loaded after the jingle; no simulator run played or read it and no pointer names it. More music, perhaps; not established.
The end of the unread block after the jingle.

Level record 0, the forest going out. A record: +0 play-area descriptor (here $8450 to $0450), +6 character-set descriptor ($8000 to $3000), +$0C colour map ($8800), +$0E/+$0F multicolours, +$10-+$17 the two players' start, +$18-+$44 the enemy tables, +$45-+$5D enemy paths, +$5E-+$71 ten cross addresses (five blue, five red), +$72 crosses needed, +$73 level byte, +$74 the card.
Level record 1, the cinema going out: play area $8E50, character set $8A00, colours $9200, 5 crosses.
Level record 2, the ghetto going out: play area $9850, character set $9400, colours $9C00, 5 crosses.
Level record 3, the graveyard going out: play area $A250, character set $9E00, colours $A600, 5 crosses.
Level record 4, the haunted house going out: play area $AC50, character set $A800, colours $B000, 5 crosses.
A switch is allowed only from level byte 10 on (+$73 of the record), the way back. So the manual's 'You can only SWITCH PLAYERS on the Return journey'. Then player_swap.
The ten level records' addresses by level byte (0, 2 ... $12): $7000, $7080, $7100, $7180, $7200 on the way to the haunted house, $7300, $7380, $7400, $7480, $7500 on the way back.
High bytes of level_records (the table is words from $7290).
copy_block with interrupts off and $01 = $34 (KERNAL and I/O banked out), so a return screen can come from the RAM under the KERNAL; then $01 = $36.
flash_border's 4-call timer.
Take one step off the energy bar (energy_down $59A3); every 4th call wait for raster line 16 and toggle bit 3 of the border colour, the flicker while poison or a touch drains energy.

Put glyph $AC above MASTERTRONIC'S (row 4, column 26) in red, then, when the colour at $DA5C is white, stamp the PROGRAMMED BY line on row 0 ($75E0 -> show_programmed_by): that is the title card, the only one printed in white there.
Level record 5, the haunted house on the way back: play area from $EC28 under the KERNAL (as the player left it), the house's graphics ($A800, $B000), 10 crosses: five for each player.
Level record 6, the graveyard on the way back: play area from $E828, graveyard graphics, 10 crosses.
Level record 7, the ghetto on the way back: play area from $E428, ghetto graphics, 10 crosses.
Level record 8, the cinema on the way back: play area from $E028, cinema graphics, 10 crosses.
Level record 9, the forest on the way back: play area from $7828, forest graphics, 10 crosses.
A byte of level record 9 that title_flicker overwrites by mistake (its STA should have been to $D023); it lies in record 9's unused tail.
Level record 9's cross addresses (+$5E-+$71) continued, the crosses needed (+$72 = 10) and the level byte (+$73 = $12); colour_cycle and place_crosses read them.
One step of the card_wait flicker for the title screen after a game (from game_over_wait). Its second branch stores to $7523 instead of $D023, so only $D022 ever flickers here: a slip in the copy.
Point the KERNAL's STOP vector low byte ($0328) at $EA, which disables the RUN/STOP check, then the first-time setup $5A60.

While no energy-refill countdown runs ($5A11 = 0), set the border to the current player's colour: 6 (blue) for the boy ($5A08 = 0), 10 (light red) for the girl ($5A08 = 1). This is the manual's 'current player is indicated by the border colour'. Then jump_colour_step $7FAE.
When the colour at $DA5C is white (the title card), show_programmed_by.
Crosses needed on this screen, from +$72 of the record, into $5A15; sprites 0 and 1 on.

Wait on the card until the card tune's count command sets $02FF; meanwhile, when random gives 0, toggle bit 1 of $D022 or $D023 (a flicker in the card's colours). Then start the play music (music_start).
Copy screen rows 0-1 (80 bytes from $0400) to $0200, then show_level_card.
Save screen rows 0-1 and show the card (hud_save $763F), then copy the 80 saved bytes from $0200 back to $0400: the score line and energy bar survive the card, which clears the screen.
tile_touch_b for tiles $70 up: below $70 return (solid); from $70 as $5B8D (solid underfoot).
next_screen's level byte.

Go on from the screen with level byte X (0, 2 ... $12). On the way out (X < 10) first store the finished play area for the way back (copy_block with store_descriptor, destination from screen_store). Then setup_screen X + 2. When the girl is the one playing ($5A08 = 1), swap the two players' sprite pointers and turn the border light red. From level byte 10 on (the way back) both sprites stay on; before that only the boy's.
next_screen on the way out: only the boy's sprite on.
Unreached, 38 bytes: no call, jump or absolute access names them and no simulator run executed or read them. They decode as nop nop nop nop nop ...: code or data left over from development.
game_over_wait's timers ($771C, $771D, $771E: 255 x 255 x 10 calls): how long the title stays before the high score is checked and the title card comes back.
game_over_wait's middle timer.
game_over_wait's outer timer.

game_over_wait's early return, then game_over_wait: while the border is not black, count three timers down; at the end check the high score, restore the title font, blank the colours, print the title card and play its music. With a black border, title_flicker.

game_over_wait: on the title (black border) flicker (title_flicker); otherwise count $771C, $771D and $771E down (255 x 255 x 10 calls), then high score, title font, colours off, the title card and its music.
game_over_wait's end: check the high score, the title font, colours off, the title card and its music.
game_over_wait with a black border: title_flicker.
Compare the score ($0406-$040B) with hiscore_digits ($8422) digit by digit; when higher copy it there, so the next game shows it after HI. Then reset game_over_wait's timers.
"PROGRAMMED BY DAVID AND RICHARD DARLING.", screen codes + $80, 40 bytes: one screen row.

Where the forest's screen rows 1-24 are stored for the way back (screen_store's first entry, from $0428): as loaded it already holds a copy, rewritten when the boy leaves the forest; record 9 reads its play area from $7828.
The title card: welcome, the goal and the controls. Printed by $7760 after a game ends.
The title card's text, PETSCII, printed by print_card: WELCOME TO THE GAME OF CHILLER, the goal, and the keys and joystick.
Scratch for $7EF1 (set sprite 0's X MSB).
Set sprite 0's X MSB in $D010 to A (0 or 1).

Count down the crosses still needed ($5A15, set from the level record). At zero the screen is done: sprites 0 and 1 on, and next_screen $7680 with the level byte (+$73 of the record, 0, 2 ... $12); after the last ($12) it passes $FE, which ends the game in a win.
Sprite 0's X, kept in $4516 as the start.
Sprite 0's Y, kept in $4517 as the start.
Sprite 0's X MSB, kept in $4518.

The boy or girl on a cross tile ($57). Reads the tile's colour (the colour-RAM cell at the same offset, $D4 pages up): bit 2 clear is a blue cross, set is red. The boy ($5A08 = 0) takes only blue crosses and the girl only red, as the manual says; the other colour is left alone. A cross taken is replaced by a space and counted by cross_count $5B5E.

Every 40th call ($5A16 counts down from $28): for each of the ten colour-RAM cells listed at +$5E..+$71 of the level record (zp $11), subtract 8 from its colour. That toggles the multicolour bit, so the ten magic crosses flash. The list is the positions of the screen's crosses.
The jump or fall step (jump_step $538E), then the colour cycle of the crosses (colour_cycle $7F80).
copy_block descriptor for next_screen: screen rows 1-24 ($0428-$07EF) to the store; next_screen patches the destination ($7FE4/$7FE5).

Where each outward screen is kept for the way back, by level byte: $7800 (forest), $E000 (cinema), $E400 (ghetto), $E800 (graveyard), $EC00 (house), then 0. The return records read their play areas from here, so the way back shows each screen as it was left: crosses taken, mushrooms eaten.

RAM the game never writes (VICE's power-on pattern). Only placeholder operands ($BBBB) in unused code point here.
A few loaded bytes in the $FF fill after the level data; unread.
Launch sprite 7 from enemy slot X if that slot's sprite is on and not dying ($CA70): direction $454E,x, then extra_launch. These bytes also serve random as the start of its table.

When the scroll period $4555 is not $FF, count $CF43 down and on zero scroll the play area (scroll_wait) with the 38-column border; every 8th count nudge the boy (scroll_nudge). Never active: every level has $FF.
Put the boy at the start the record gave (Y from $4517, X from $4516, MSB from $4518), his colour ($4510 into $D027), then new_life $CAED.
Screen utilities that only other unused code calls ($51CF, $526C): fill routines for the screen and colour RAM, a glyph mirror ($C150), a 64-byte clear. Left from development.
Read as data by random, whose table runs on from $C000 through $C0FF; as code it is the rest of unused_screen_tools, which nothing calls.
The enemy slot spawn_enemy is placing.

Bring enemy slot A (0-4, on sprites 2-6) onto the screen: mark it moving (mark_moving), put it on its path (enemy_to_path), sprite on (its bit from $CF46), first frame from $CF68 into its pointer ($07FA,x), its colour and first direction ($C6E0 -> set_enemy_colour).

A bit table $80 ... $01 and a screen-clear loop, called only by unused_screen_tools. Not reached in play: no simulator run on any of the ten screens read or ran it, and the only instructions that name it are the card text read as code ($41xx-$43xx), the unused tools, or the RAM under the KERNAL.
place_boy continued: X, the MSB ($C1E1), then colour and new_life.

Jump direction: 0 rising, 1 falling.
1 while the boy is in the air, 0 on the ground.

Fire or SHIFT was pressed. Where the level allows jumping ($45FF = 1) start a jump (start_jump $5418) unless the boy is already in the air ($C19C). Where it does not ($45FF = 0) fire brings in the second player (switch_check $C7D4). Then walk_frame.

An older joystick reader nothing calls: turns $DC00's bits into -1/0/+1 in X and Y.

Horizontal direction from read_controls: $FF left, 1 right, 0 none; held through a jump.
1 when fire or SHIFT was pressed this read.

Copy bytes from (zp $FB) to (zp $FD) until the source reaches the end in $0390/$0391. copy_block rewrites the immediates at $C29E-$C2B3 before each use; as the image holds them they copy the HUD rows $8400-$844F to $0400.

High bytes of the same table. Like the tune, its pitches land on equal temperament at the NTSC clock.
Move enemy sprite X in direction Y: move_sprite with A = Y.
Unreached: the next byte of a note list at $4000 ($0380 as index), $00 stops, $FC-$FF silence, others are notes from freq_lo/freq_hi. Every SID store is to $FFFF.

Saved character of the play area's first cell, for scroll_left.
Scroll the play area (rows 1-24 and their colours) one cell to the left, the first cell wrapping round. Reached only through scroll_timer, which every level switches off ($4555 = $FF).
Wait for raster line $4B, then scroll_left and scroll_rows.
The second half of the scroll: each row's last cell moves down a row (from $07BF up), then the saved cell goes back.

A colour copy into the HUD (sprite colours to colour RAM, $C4D4); named only by unreached code at $2EF1 and by level data. Not reached in play: no simulator run on any of the ten screens read or ran it, and the only instructions that name it are the card text read as code ($41xx-$43xx), the unused tools, or the RAM under the KERNAL.

Sprite 1 against the scenery (collect_check, $D01F bit 1) on screens with $45FE set: A = 1 switches sprite 1 off; otherwise it flips sprite 1's frame and after 5 flips ($C544) switches it off. No level record sets $45FE (it reads 0), so it never runs.
Every 8th scroll count, move sprite 0 left and down one pixel with try_move.
Counts sprite1_hit_scenery's frame flips (to 5).

A dying slot's animation: every 10 passes ($CF82,x) and every $455B,x of those, the next frame; at frame $FC the sprite goes off and the slot is free ($CF4F,x = 0).

A new game: reset the players and score (reset_players, boy_first), the background colour ($450F), a CHR$(8) to lock the character set, sprites off; setup_screen 0 (the operand at $C661 is the starting level byte), the HUD rows from $8400 (hud_descriptor), then into restart_screen.

Start (or restart) play on the current screen: spawn the level's first enemies ($45AB = 0: spawn_enemy $C0E4 for slots 0 to $45AC-1), put the boy back at his start (place_boy $C032), the play font ($D018 = $1C), sprite 7 frame $F8 and sprite 1's colour, clear the enemies' timers, read $D01E to clear it, then enemy_setup $2D00 and main_loop.
Busy-wait $CF66 times $CF65 loops. Registers kept.
Every 8th pass: move sprite 1 one pixel through move_sprite $C900 (X = 1), taking its frame number ($07F9 - $E0) as the direction. Its result is not used.
joy_move's end.

Every 32nd pass: read the controls (read_controls $C84D), then move the boy one pixel per direction held through try_move $2A04. $C1EC is vertical and $C1ED horizontal ($FF up or left, 1 down or right). Each direction is allowed only when the level's flag says so ($4500-$4503: up, down, left, right) and animates when $4504-$4507 say so, choosing sprite 0's frame ($07F8, $D8-$DF). $CF06 counts the moves. With fire or SHIFT ($C1EE) goes to fire_pressed $C19D; then walk_frame $C819.
The frame bases player_input adds for walking left and right ($D8, $DC; $E0 in a jump; $E8, $EC for the girl), then the rest of player_input.
player_input's frame base for walking right ($DC, patched), then fire.

Fire on a screen without jumping: when sprite 1 is off ($D015 bit 1 clear), bring it in on top of the boy with the frame for the current facing from $4508 (+$E0), sprite 1 on, its MSB bit copied from sprite 0, and voice 3 loaded from $45B3 ($2F00). With sprite 1 already on, nothing.
Advance the walking animation when the boy moved this pass ($CF06) or always when $450D = 1: every $450C calls ($CF07) step sprite 0's frame (frame_step). Its first byte becomes RTS during a jump.
walk_frame's return when nothing moved.
The end of walk_frame after its NOPs; reached only through operands the card text holds ($5EEF, $5EF5 are LDA (zp),Y there, not jumps).

Turn the keyboard and the port-2 joystick into directions: $C1EC vertical, $C1ED horizontal ($FF up/left, 1 down/right, 0 none), $C1EE = 1 to jump. Keys come from the KERNAL's key code in $C5 ($40 = none) compared with the level's key table $4512-$4515 (SPACE, SPACE, Z, C: Z walks left, C right, live); SHIFT from the KERNAL's shift flag $028D; the stick from $DC00 through read_stick ($C9C4): up (bit 0) sets $C1EE like SHIFT, down, left and right set the directions. With $4511 = 1 the last direction is kept while nothing is pressed. Its first byte is switched between LDA # ($A9) and RTS ($60) by $5821 and $588B: a jump in progress disables it.

Move sprite X (0-7) one pixel in direction A: 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right. Limits: Y from $32 to $E3, X from 8 (MSB clear) to $14F (MSB set). Keeps $D010's bit for the sprite with bit_clear_mask and bit_set_mask. Returns Y = 0 when it moved, $FF at an edge. Used for the boy, the girl and every enemy.
Unreached, 42 bytes: no call, jump or absolute access names them and no simulator run executed or read them. They decode as nop nop nop inc ldx ...: code or data left over from development.
Return $DC00 (the port-2 joystick) in A. If the stick is pushed and no key is down, first clear both remembered directions, so the stick replaces a key direction.
Eight masks with one bit clear ($FE, $FD ... $7F): AND with $D010 to clear sprite n's X MSB.
Eight single-bit masks ($01, $02 ... $80): sprite n's bit in $D010.

The game's random number: the next byte of the code at $C000 (index $CF14, incremented each call) EOR zp $A2. Returns it in Y, and X = $20. Used for enemy movement, the extra enemy's timing, respawns and the title colour flicker.

The main loop of play; it never returns. Each pass: tick_border $75B0 (the border back to the player's colour, then the jump/fall step and the colour cycle), player_step $5800 (the boy's walking frame, energy and crosses), joy_move $C700 every 8th pass, player_input $C71B every 32nd pass ($CF03 counts to $20). Then collect_check $2D4B, which goes on to enemy_pass $CA27, which comes back here.
main_loop's joy_move period (8, patched from $45FD), the input period at $CA19, player_input, then collect_check.
main_loop's input period ($20, patched to $80 by bar_speed when tired, and from $45FC), then player_input.

Second half of the main loop. enemy_step $CDE9 for each enemy slot 0-4, extra_enemy $CCF5 (the flyer on sprite 7), sprite_touch $CE87 (the boy's collisions). $CF81 = 1 means the screen was left: restart_screen $C694. Otherwise the scroll timer $C011 and the respawn timer $2FB2; $CF7F = $FF (RUN/STOP was pressed) quits to end_game $2CB4, else back to main_loop.
Move enemy sprite X (2-6) in direction Y with move_sprite (via $C37A), only when its $D015 bit is on.

A note player that nothing in play reaches (respawn's $2FAC and the unused $2C3A call it). It steps through 32 notes at $458B, each an index into the split frequency table $C300/$C340, 8 steps per frame of sprite 0's pointer. Every SID store in it has the operand $FFFF, in the PRG as loaded too: the sound was cut before release.
Take a life ($CF7C), boy's sprite only, reload the enemies' lives (enemy_lives $56BC).

The slot enemy_to_path is placing.

Place enemy slot A on its path: $CF0D,x gives the slot's five-byte block in the path table $4519 (X, Y, MSB bit, a count right, a count down). The sprite goes to that X, Y and MSB, then is walked right (move_sprite direction 3) and down (direction 1) by a random part of each count (random), so each spawn lands at a random point along a line.
The slot path_step is moving.

Move enemy slot A one pixel in its direction ($CF15,x, 0-3) with move_sprite (sprite A + 2). At an edge, unless the slot is allowed to stop there ($4538,x), it leaves the screen: enemy_gone and sprite off. Every 8 steps ($CF1A) the next direction: from its path script (pointer $575E,x / $CF24,x, index $CF29,x; $FF restarts), or, when $453D,x is set, a random one of the script's first 64.
path_step continued: move the enemy (enemy_move_if_on); at an edge remove it unless $4538 lets it stay; otherwise count to its next turn.

Every $CF9C,x passes (the move delay that speed_up halves each LEVEL) take a path step (path_step). Every 16 passes ($CF97) and every $54E5,x of those, step the sprite's frame, wrapping from the last ($CF38,x) to the first ($CF3D,x).
The thrown extra enemy on sprite 7. While it is off, now and then (extra_roll below $4553 = 16) launch it from a random enemy slot 0-4 (launch_extra). While it is on, extra_move.
Direction A (4 means this slot throws nothing) into $CF44; sprite 7 on at slot X's position (sprite X+2's X, Y and MSB), colour $454D.
Every $4554 (16) passes ($CF45) move sprite 7 one pixel in its direction ($CF44); at an edge switch it off.
Returns Y = a random 0-127 only when a second roll is at least $78, else $7F: a launch needs two rolls.
Sprite 1 (the character not under control, standing where it was left) touching any enemy sprite also loses energy (poison_add X = 2).

Nothing reaches this; it opens with three undocumented one-byte NOPs ($DA). It would score an enemy hit by a shot: its slot from $CF4D, and when $4556,x allows, kill it ($CF4F,x = 1, sprite 1 off, points from add_score_for); otherwise lose energy. Chiller has no shot, so this is left from the engine it was built on.
unused_shot_hit's return when the enemy may not be hit.
One enemy slot's turn in enemy_pass: dying ($CF4F,x = 1) runs enemy_dying; otherwise enemy_move.
unused_shot_hit continued: a dying enemy is left alone; otherwise the boy loses energy.
One point: add 1 to the score's last digit ($040B) and carry leftwards through the six digits at $0406-$040B (glyphs $B0-$B9).
One point off the score, with borrow, then score_inc: a net change of 0 for the digit it starts on. Nothing calls it.
Add $CF5A + 255 x $CF5B points, one at a time. $CF5C is written into the JSR at $CE52 as its low byte ($11 makes it JSR score_inc), so a caller could pick another counter.
add_score's patched JSR target ($11: score_inc), then the loop over the points.
Points for enemy $CF4E: $4560,x units, $4565,x times 255 more, and $456A,x as the add_score call target. Reached only from unused code ($CE0D, $2FA3, and $090D in the loader's area).
add_score_for: the points of enemy $CF4E, then add_score.

Reached only from $CAF9, itself unused: a life off ($CAED), the digit at $041A down, and at 0 the screen-over flag $CF7D.

RAM under the KERNAL where next_screen stores the cinema's rows 1-24 when the boy leaves it (screen_store), written with the KERNAL banked in (a write goes to the RAM beneath).
